Gantron College Basketball 2026-27

Updated Sun Nov 1, 8:57 PM CT
About the Model
20,000 simulated seasons per run: every game left is played out from the two teams' ratings and home court, and each conference's regular-season standings decide its title. A rating is points per game better than an average Division I team on a neutral court, so the gap between two teams is the expected margin. A shared title counts as a title on this page; Kalshi pays a shared title at its share. 2,403 Kalshi markets priced. Model version 0.1.0.

Rating = how many points per game better a team is than an average Division I team on a neutral court; tap a team for its card.

Column Guide
RatingRtgpoints per game better than an average Division I team on a neutral court; the gap between two teams is the expected margin
OffenseOffpoints scored per 100 possessions against an average defense; higher is better
DefenseDefpoints allowed per 100 possessions against an average offense; lower is better
Tempopossessions per 40 minutes
Projected RecordW-Lexpected wins and losses over the whole regular season
Projected Conf RecordConf W-LCW-Lexpected conference wins and losses
80% RangeRangehow far the team's true rating could be from its listed one: 8 times in 10 it is within this many points. Wider for teams we know less about (more roster turnover); it narrows for every team as the season goes
Luckpoints per game the team's shooting luck has been worth so far: opponents' threes and free throws against what those shooters usually make, and its own threes against its usual rate (+ = the luck helped). The rating takes out the part that will not repeat, about a fifth. The hover and the team card also show close-game luck (wins beyond what its game-by-game margins earned), which moves the rating a little the other way, and each part's rating change. Shown from a team's 5th game
Tipstap a team for its card; tap a header to sort; the small numbers are ranks

Each conference's projected regular-season standings and each team's chance to win or share the title, from 20,000 simulated seasons.

Column Guide
Race bareach team's slice of the regular-season title in its colors: a shared title is split between the co-champions, so the slices add up to 100%
#projected finish, by expected conference wins
RatingRtgpoints per game better than an average Division I team
Projected Conf RecordConf W-Lexpected conference wins and losses
Solo ChampionSoloour chance to finish first in the regular-season standings ALONE, with fair American odds
Co-ChampionCoour chance to TIE for first (the league names co-champions)
More columnsadds Kalshi Fair and Kalshi Edge
Kalshi Fairwhat a Kalshi regular-season title contract is worth to us: it pays 1 for a solo title and 1/N for a share of N co-champions, so this is the number to compare with the Kalshi price
Kalshi Edgeour edge after fees on the better side, in cents: Win = backing the team for the regular-season title, Not Win = betting against it; Kalshi lists these titles for the ACC, Big 12, Big East, Big Ten and SEC. Grey with * = a thin market (little volume or an old quote): the price may not be there
Tiptap a team or its slice of the bar for its card

Each conference tournament played through its own bracket, seeded by the league's tiebreakers: each team's projected seed, its chance to make the field, reach the final and win the title (and the automatic bid), from 12,000 simulated seasons.

Column Guide
Race bareach team's slice of the tournament title, in its colors
#projected seed order
Projected SeedSeedthe team's average seed over the simulated seasons, by the league's own tiebreakers
Make FieldFieldthe chance to qualify, in leagues where not every team plays
Reach FinalFinalthe chance to play in the title game
Win TourneyWinthe chance to win the tournament (the automatic bid's usual route; Kalshi's conference-tournament markets settle on it), with fair American odds
More columnsadds Kalshi Edge: our edge after fees on the better side, in cents (Win = backing the team to win the tournament, Not Win = betting against it), and Final Edge where Kalshi lists a reach-the-final market (Win = backing the team to reach it)
Tiptap a team or its slice of the bar for its card

Column Guide

No. 1 Seed1 Seedour chance to be one of the four No. 1 seeds
Roundsour chance to reach each round: the Round of 32, the Sweet 16, the Elite 8, the Final Four, the title game, and to win it all (with American odds)
Contenders / AllContenders lists teams with a 1% or better chance to make the field
Tiptap a team for its card; tap a header to sort
